subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram setup move from pairing by default to token-verified owner capture that writes `dmPolicy="allowlist"` and `allowFrom`, while preserving explicit pairing-mode configs?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but it changes Telegram first-run trust, owner identity capture, and default authorization behavior for a security-sensitive channel.

options.title: Token-verified allowlist bootstrap
options.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to DM that token, then persist the matching numeric Telegram user ID as allowFrom for fresh setups while preserving explicit configs.

options.title: Post-bootstrap auto-flip
options.body: Keep first-run pairing, then adopt the broader open follow-up that derives allowlist behavior after commands.ownerAllowFrom is populated.

options.title: Keep pairing default
options.body: Leave pairing as the default and rely on warnings/manual allowlist setup, accepting the current stranger-pairing-request exposure.

recommendation.title: Token-verified allowlist bootstrap
recommendation.body: Generate a short setup token, require the intended owner to DM that token, then persist the matching numeric Telegram user ID as allowFrom for fresh setups while preserving explicit configs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent Telegram runtime/docs/config history and prior review context for this security-default decision.
